title: Unit-frame interval sieve: O(n^4 2^((9/2) sqrt n)) DCP for every N

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the unit-frame interval sieve UFIS-9/2 of proof.md (b = ceil(2 sqrt n) and all constants as in its Section 1), with n = ceil(log2 N), recovers the entire s with unconditional probability > 3/4. In the challenge model its worst-case total work is T(N,s) = O(n^4 2^((9/2) sqrt(n))), with an absolute hidden constant and the explicit exponent coefficient 9/2; the envelope B_T(n) = 2^((9/2) n^(1/2)) n^4 has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds, on every execution branch (fixed copy counts, no restarts; aborts only stop early), and with unconditional full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the unit-frame interval sieve UFIS-9/2 of proof.md (b = ceil(2 sqrt n) and all constants as in its Section 1), with n = ceil(log2 N), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n 2^((9/2) sqrt(n))) bits, absolute hidden constant. The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((9/2) n^(1/2)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds, on every execution branch (fixed copy counts, no restarts; aborts only stop early), and with unconditional full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the unit-frame interval sieve UFIS-9/2 of proof.md (b = ceil(2 sqrt n) and all constants as in its Section 1), with n = ceil(log2 N), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^((9/2) sqrt(n))) qubits, absolute hidden constant. The envelope B_Q(n) = 2^((9/2) n^(1/2)) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds, on every execution branch (fixed copy counts, no restarts; aborts only stop early), and with unconditional full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the unit-frame interval sieve UFIS-9/2 of proof.md (b = ceil(2 sqrt n) and all constants as in its Section 1), with n = ceil(log2 N), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch is Q(N,s) <= 4 m M_0 (or m(p+1)2^(p+5)t in the bounded-n case d = 0) = O(n 2^((9/2) sqrt(n))), including all discarded copies. The envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((9/2) n^(1/2)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds, on every execution branch (fixed copy counts, no restarts; aborts only stop early), and with unconditional full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the same algorithm UFIS-9/2 and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability > 3/4 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
